title: Resume + Retry Strategy and Backpressure Proofing — Streaming Outage Follow-up
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: During a capacity spike on 2026-03-09 we observed widespread streaming response failures manifesting as abrupt client disconnects, truncated/partial token streams, and noisy retries that amplified load. This ticket captures the post-incident findings and the actionable work to make streaming more resilient: specifically a robust resume+retry protocol, connection-level flow-control hardening, and safeguards for KV-cache induced latency spikes.

Problem statement: Three coupling failures combined to cause the outage: (1) the current streaming resume behavior was non-idempotent and relied on best-effort token reconciliation; retries frequently produced duplicate or partial outputs and caused clients to reconnect more aggressively; (2) the batching subsystem reacted to transient KV-cache misses by increasing batch sizes, which elevated tail latency and triggered upstream backpressure without clear per-connection damping; (3) our flow-control signals are coarse-grained (per-pool) rather than per-connection, which allowed a small number of slow connections to stall worker fill rates.

Detection and impact: The outage surfaced as increased 5xx stream termination rates, sharp rise in reconnects per-second, and a spike in token re-generation in logs. Affected customers experienced partial message delivery and higher latency for new requests. Root analysis used tracing across stream lifecycles, per-token timestamps, and batch occupancy heatmaps.

Primary findings: 
- Resume markers were implemented as a best-effort sequence number in the client adapter; there was no server-side guarantee of idempotent replay.
- Retry logic retriggered full request evaluation rather than resuming from a checkpoint when KV cache warmed, causing duplicate token emission.
- Batcher adaptive sizing increased in reaction to KV cache misses (to amortize kernel startup), but lacked a cap tied to latency SLOs.
- Flow-control is currently enforced by a global token budget per worker pool; slow TCP clients could consume that budget indirectly leading to head-of-line stalls.

Action items (short-term / hotfix, owners, target dates):
1) Implement a conservative resume handshake that exchanges a stable resume token and last-acked-token-index; fallback path keeps original disconnect semantics. Owner: Kenji Sato. Due: 2026-03-18. Acceptance: resume handshake exercised by end-to-end integration tests and no duplicate tokens in 95th percentile test runs.
2) Add server-side idempotency checks for resumed sessions: keep per-session last-output hash for 60s, detect and drop overlapping replay. Owner: Priya Nayar. Due: 2026-03-16. Acceptance: regression tests assert no duplicate tokens emitted during resume.
3) Temporary throttle on automatic batch inflation: cap adaptive batch growth to maintain 99th latency under SLO. Owner: Rafael Ortiz. Due: 2026-03-15. Acceptance: benchmark with synthetic KV-miss workload demonstrates 99th latency within target.
4) Short-term per-connection soft flow-control token buckets in the gateway to prevent a slow connection from blocking worker fill. Owner: Mei Chen. Due: 2026-03-17. Acceptance: simulated slow-client test reduces head-of-line stalls by >80%.

Action items (medium-term):
5) Design and implement a streaming session state machine persisted in a lightweight in-memory store so resume tokens are authoritative and consistent across failovers. Owner: Kenji Sato + Storage team. Due: 2026-04-14. Acceptance: can resume across control plane failover in staging.
6) Rework batching policy to include latency-aware caps and per-model sequence-length profiles so batcher chooses size with an SLO objective (latency vs throughput). Owner: Rafael Ortiz. Due: 2026-04-21. Acceptance: new scheduler reduces cost without increasing latency for production traces.
7) KV-cache warmup: proactively fetch likely prefixes for active sessions when resume token is seen; instrument cache warmup hit rate. Owner: Priya Nayar. Due: 2026-04-07. Acceptance: cache warmup raises hit rate for resumed sessions by >=25%.

Action items (long-term / research):
8) Evaluate signed-sum token hashing to make token-level deduplication robust across quantized model outputs. Owner: Research team (assign Q2). Due: 2026-06-30.
9) Explore transport-layer improvements: HTTP/2 window tuning, explicit per-stream backpressure frames, and potential WebTransport adoption. Owner: Network Infra. Due: 2026-07-15. Acceptance: proposal with benchmarks.

Testing and rollout plan: All short-term items will be feature-flagged. Hotfixes (items 1–4) will be deployed first to staging, followed by Canary (10% traffic) for 48h telemetry check, then 100% rollout. Post-rollout monitoring includes: per-session resume success rate, duplicate-token incidents, reconnect rate, batch-size distribution, and 95/99 token latency.

Open questions / trade-offs: 
- How long to retain per-session resume metadata vs memory cost? (currently proposing 60s; need ops input).
- Should resume handshake be mandatory for all clients or opt-in behind feature flag? Opt-in reduces blast radius but prolongs old-client pain.
- Risk: server-side idempotency could drop legitimate partial replays if hashes collide; mitigation is conservative hash window and replay log.

Expected customer communication: A brief incident summary and high-level mitigation plan will be posted to the incident page and sent to affected customers by Customer Success; detailed technical postmortem will be published after medium-term items are validated.
updates: 2026-03-11: Initial RCA complete; created ticket and assigned owners for hotfixes.
2026-03-12: Kenji prototyped resume handshake; integration tests added to CI pipeline.
2026-03-13: Priya implemented server-side last-output hash for quick dedupe; unit tests passing.
2026-03-14: Rafael pushed throttling cap to test branch; load tests scheduled for 2026-03-15.
2026-03-14: Mei added gateway-level per-connection buckets behind flag; canary config ready.
